nodes.name: POST /lead
nodes.notes: Entry point. {"domain": "acme.com", "idempotency_key": "<optional>"} with an X-Auth-Token header. Responds via Respond-to-Webhook nodes so every exit path returns an explicit, typed status.

nodes.name: Validate & Derive Key
nodes.notes: Auth gate + domain normalisation + idempotency key derivation (§4.7, §4.1).

nodes.name: Authorized & valid?
nodes.notes: Rejects before touching Postgres or the API — no DB write, no LLM spend.

nodes.name: Reject 401 / 400

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ error: $json.authorized ? 'invalid_domain' : 'unauthorized', detail: $json.authorized ? 'body.domain is missing or not a domain' : 'missing or wrong X-Auth-Token header' }) }}

nodes.notes: 401 for a bad token, 400 for a malformed domain.

nodes.name: Acquire Idempotency Key

parameters.query:
-- §4.1 Idempotency acquisition: ONE atomic statement, never check-then-insert.
-- Two concurrent submissions of the same key cannot both pass here.
--   * fresh key            -> row inserted, xmax = 0     -> outcome 'acquired_new'
--   * key exists, 'failed' -> reset to in_progress       -> outcome 'acquired_retry'
--   * key exists, 'completed' or 'in_progress'
--                          -> ON CONFLICT WHERE fails, ZERO rows returned.
-- Zero rows is the signal that a concurrent caller owns the key; the next node
-- reads its current status. That read is race-free because the row is
-- guaranteed to exist once this statement has returned.
INSERT INTO idempotency_keys (key, domain, status)
VALUES ($1, $2, 'in_progress')
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE
   SET status     = 'in_progress',
       updated_at = now()
 WHERE idempotency_keys.status = 'failed'
RETURNING key,
          CASE WHEN xmax = 0 THEN 'acquired_new' ELSE 'acquired_retry' END AS outcome;

nodes.notes:
§4.1 — the single atomic statement. alwaysOutputData is ON so the zero-row 'someone else holds this key' case still produces an item to branch on.

Select the 'Lead Qualifier Postgres' credential on this node after import.

nodes.name: Key acquired?
nodes.notes: A returned row means we own the work. No row means a concurrent caller does.

nodes.name: Read Existing Key

parameters.query:
-- We lost the race for this key. Read who holds it and in what state.
SELECT key, domain, status, result
  FROM idempotency_keys
 WHERE key = $1;

nodes.notes:
Race-free: the conflicting row is guaranteed to exist now that the upsert returned.

Select the 'Lead Qualifier Postgres' credential on this node after import.

nodes.name: Cached or in flight?
nodes.notes: Terminal 'completed' returns the stored result. Anything else is still in flight.

nodes.name: Respond 200 Cached
nodes.notes: §4.1 — returns the stored result and STOPS. This branch deliberately does not reach the routing Switch: re-submitting a lead must never re-fire the hot path.

nodes.name: Respond 409 In Flight

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ error: 'duplicate_in_flight', idempotency_key: $json.key, detail: 'this key is already being processed' }) }}

nodes.notes: Duplicate while the first run is still working.

nodes.name: Call /qualify
nodes.notes: §4.8 timeout arithmetic: enrichment 8s + up to 3 LLM attempts x 20s = 68s worst case, so the node timeout is set explicitly to 75s rather than left at the default. neverError + fullResponse hand every status code to the evaluator; the error output catches real transport failures. x-trace-id = the idempotency key, which is what correlates n8n executions with the API's structured_logs rows (§4.5).

nodes.name: Evaluate Attempt
nodes.notes: Judges one attempt and decides whether it is worth repeating (§4.2).

nodes.name: Qualified?
nodes.notes: 200 with a valid payload, or not.

nodes.name: Retry transport?
nodes.notes: §4.2 transport layer: 3 attempts total, 5xx/network only. Deliberately separate from the API's schema-repair retry, which changes the prompt instead of re-sending an identical request.

nodes.name: Exponential backoff
nodes.notes: 2s, then 4s. Feeds straight back into Call /qualify; $runIndex is what carries the attempt count around the loop.

nodes.name: Mark Completed

parameters.query:
-- Terminal state. A 'completed' key is never re-run and never re-routed,
-- so a duplicate submission cannot re-fire the hot-path side effect (§4.1).
UPDATE idempotency_keys
   SET status     = 'completed',
       result     = $2::jsonb,
       updated_at = now()
 WHERE key = $1
RETURNING key, status, updated_at;

nodes.notes:
Stores the result so a replay of this key short-circuits to the cached branch.

Select the 'Lead Qualifier Postgres' credential on this node after import.

nodes.name: Route by score
nodes.notes: Routes on `tier`, not on a number. The hot>=70 / warm 40-69 / cold<40 cutoffs live in exactly one place — Thresholds in config.py — so they are never duplicated into this node (§8). n8n still owns what each tier DOES; the API only owns where the lines are. Cold is the fallback output, so an unexpected tier degrades to the branch with no side effects.

nodes.name: Hot: action configured?
nodes.notes: §8 — the real hot-path action activates only if LQ_HOT_PATH_WEBHOOK_URL is set. Nobody needs a Slack workspace to run the demo, and the extension point is real rather than hypothetical.

nodes.name: Hot: notify

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ text: 'Hot lead: ' + $('Evaluate Attempt').first().json.domain + ' (score ' + $('Evaluate Attempt').first().json.body.score.score + ')', domain: $('Evaluate Attempt').first().json.domain, score: $('Evaluate Attempt').first().json.body.score.score, draft_message: $('Evaluate Attempt').first().json.body.score.draft_message }) }}

nodes.notes: Same graceful-degradation rule as enrichment: a dead Slack hook must not sink an otherwise-qualified lead, so failure continues rather than throwing.

nodes.name: Hot: no action configured
nodes.notes: Hot path with no webhook configured — the documented default.

nodes.name: Warm: nurture
nodes.notes: Warm band (40-69). Extension point for a nurture sequence.

nodes.name: Cold: archive
nodes.notes: Cold band (<40) and the fallback for any unexpected tier. No side effects.

nodes.name: Respond 200 Qualified
nodes.notes: Returns the API's own validated payload verbatim — n8n never reshapes the domain contract.

nodes.name: Classify Failure
nodes.notes: Maps the failure onto the dead_letters.failure_stage CHECK constraint (§4.4).

nodes.name: Dead Letter & Mark Failed

parameters.query:
-- §4.4 Dead-letter write and idempotency demotion in one statement, so we can
-- never end up with a dead letter whose key still reads 'in_progress'.
-- 'failed' is retryable: a later submission of the same key re-acquires it.
WITH dl AS (
  INSERT INTO dead_letters
    (domain, idempotency_key, failure_stage, last_error, attempt_count, payload_snapshot)
  VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6::jsonb)
  RETURNING id
)
UPDATE idempotency_keys
   SET status     = 'failed',
       updated_at = now()
 WHERE key = $2
RETURNING key, status, (SELECT id FROM dl) AS dead_letter_id;

nodes.notes:
One statement: a dead letter can never exist beside a key still reading 'in_progress'.

Select the 'Lead Qualifier Postgres' credential on this node after import.

nodes.name: Respond Typed Error

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ error: 'qualification_failed', stage: $('Classify Failure').first().json.failure_stage, detail: $('Classify Failure').first().json.last_error, attempts: $('Classify Failure').first().json.attempt_count, dead_letter_id: $json.dead_letter_id, idempotency_key: $('Classify Failure').first().json.idempotency_key }) }}

nodes.notes: Passes the API's typed status through (422 / 502 / 503) instead of flattening everything to 500, and hands back the dead-letter id so the failure is immediately greppable in Postgres.
